correctness.rationale: Independent replay confirms the full headline table. (a) Scope fidelity: all 22 embedded 36-char strings are valid 6x6 Latin squares, pairwise distinct, and byte-identical in order to live McKay latin_is6.txt fetched 2026-09-08 (22 lines match). (b) Transversal counts: fresh stdlib permutation scan over all 720 diagonals per square reproduces T=(32,0,8,0,0,24,24,8,0,8,0,24,8,8,8,8,0,0,0,0,8,0) exactly; verify.py prints per-type OK. (c) Packing numbers: every stored witness family is a set of p column-perms each with distinct symbols (hence transversals), contained in the enumerated transversal list, and pairwise cell-disjoint; exhaustive C(T,p+1) scan (worst C(32,5)=201376 on Type 1, C(24,5)=42504 on Types 6,7,12, C(8,5)/C(8,3)=56 elsewhere, trivial at T=0) proves no (p+1)-family exists, so p=(4,0,4,0,0,4,4,2,0,2,0,4,2,4,4,2,0,0,0,0,4,0) is optimal. Hence p_max=4 on exactly {1,3,6,7,12,14,15,21} and all p<6 consistent with Euler/Tarry. (d) Hall-Paige labels: independent exhaustive isotopy search (720 row-perms x 720 col-perms, symbol map forced by first row) against Z6 and S3 -- the only groups of order 6 up to isomorphism -- finds hits only at Type 2 ~= Z6 and Type 4 ~= S3; auditor reproduced this full scan (22x2x518k candidates with early exit) yielding nongroup for the other 20 types and verified the two stored isotopy witnesses satisfy s[L[r[i]][c[j]]]==G[i][j]. Group-table zeros T=p=0 are consistent with Hall-Paige (both groups have cyclic/nontrivial Sylow 2-subgroups). Evidence is deductive proof by finite exhaustive enumeration with deterministic stdlib replay, not sampling or heuristic search; boundary cases T=0/p=0 handled vacuously and correctly. Presentation honestly discloses file-order numbering, computational (not structural) group labels, and brute-force optimality certificates.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison against nearest priors shows no published per-type (T_i,p_i) packing spectrum over the complete 22-type order-6 isotopy classification. Best-Pula-Wanless (1911.05936) proves by computation that every Latin array of order n<=11 has diagonal weight >=n-1 (one near-transversal existence); it gives no transversal counts, no packing numbers p, no per-isotopy distribution. Montgomery survey (2406.19873, 26pp) and Wanless survey (0903.5142) are asymptotic/structural/survey with enumeration discussion but no (T_i,p_i) table or extremal-type set over all 22 order-6 types. Kazemi-Pahlavsay (1808.05213) states the maximum number of disjoint transversals as a famous open problem with mate/quasi-transversal theory only -- motivation, not anticipation. Cavenagh-Wanless (1609.03001) counts transversal-free species asymptotically, no finite per-type census. Potapov (1506.01577) gives only an asymptotic lower bound on max transversals. McKay latin data + OEIS A040082 supply only the 22 representatives and type counts (1,1,1,2,2,22,564,...), no transversal invariants; auditor confirmed the live files contain matrices only. Hall-Paige literature (group complete mappings) mechanically implies only the two group-table zeros (Types 2,4); the 20 nongroup counts, the full p-distribution, p_max=4, and the named 8-element extremal set are not implied. arXiv API queries (transversal+order-6, transversal+isotopy, packing-number+transversal) returned only the above asymptotic/structural/existence results, none with the claimed table. Timestamp/failed-search alone is not cited as proof; the comparison is claim-by-claim. Novelty is isolated correctly in DRAFT (only 2 zeros conceded as implied).

value.rationale: The headline claim is a rigorously established exact invariant of a specific natural object meeting the narrow-datum value clause: object = complete McKay 22-type isotopy classification of order-6 Latin squares (closed classical Euler/Tarry boundary, fixed before computation, no seeding); invariant = full (T_i,p_i) spectrum plus p_max=4 with exact 8-type extremal set and Hall-Paige group-vs-nongroup split, with explicit disjoint-family witnesses and exhaustive optimality certificates replayable from matrices alone. Motivation predates computation (maximum disjoint transversals as recognized open problem per Kazemi; order 6 as no-mate boundary with unknown packing distribution; stated downstream use as ground truth for rainbow-matching/packing solvers). Values were not known or mechanically implied (only 2/22 entries implied by Hall-Paige; rest computed; distributions T in {0:10,8:8,24:3,32:1}, p in {0:10,2:4,4:8} not guessable). A future researcher could reasonably need the precise per-type table, witness families, or extremal-type identities. This is a complete census over a natural scope, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration; certification strengthens but does not substitute for the substantive gap. Judged as headline exact result, it does not require a new general theorem, completed broader census, or already-used downstream theorem.

Group-based labels rest on computational isotopy search with stored witnesses, not a structural derivation (disclosed; witnesses are checkable).
Optimality certificates are brute-force exact scans with no closed-form theorem; correctness depends on machine replay (deterministic stdlib, seconds-scale, re-executed by auditor).
No statement beyond order 6 or beyond these representatives is supported; mate-existence and near-transversal results correctly conceded to Tarry / Best et al.
